blocked_records.context: An unidentified voice or group answers Raphael's call to action.
blocked_records.source_meaning: The speaker gives an enthusiastic affirmative shout.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}Buy low, sell high. That is how trade works.{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio begins the trading tutorial at Lisbon's trading post.
records.source_meaning: Julio says that buying goods cheaply and selling them for more is the basic principle of trade.
records.localization_note: Uses the familiar buy-low, sell-high formulation in a complete, natural explanation.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}Sailing between the Mediterranean and Africa brings quick profits.{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio explains the long-term value of regional trade routes.
records.source_meaning: Julio says that traveling back and forth between the Mediterranean and Africa provides a quick way to make money.
records.localization_note: Uses a complete conversational explanation rather than a clipped instruction.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}Stay close to home for now. A long voyage is too much.{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio advises Raphael to start trading locally.
records.source_meaning: Julio says a distant voyage is unrealistic at the beginning and tells Raphael to test the waters close by.
records.localization_note: Stay close to home naturally conveys Julio's advice to begin with nearby markets.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}Compare prices. Seek bigger profits.{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio encourages checking local market prices.
records.source_meaning: Julio says Raphael can watch the prices in each town and try to make a large profit.
records.localization_note: Uses idiomatic trading advice while preserving Julio's encouragement to pursue a large profit within the fixed allocation.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}Buy saffron or almonds in Lisbon, then sell them near Ceuta.{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio recommends a specific beginner trade between Lisbon and Ceuta.
records.source_meaning: Julio advises buying saffron or almonds in Lisbon and selling them near Ceuta.
records.localization_note: Uses lowercase commodity names as ordinary goods and renders Julio's recommendation conversationally.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}At first, few ships and cargo holds limit how much you can trade.{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio explains the fleet's initial trading limit.
records.source_meaning: Julio says the small number of ships and cargo holds at the beginning limits how many goods can be bought or sold at one time.
records.localization_note: Little cargo space expresses the mechanical restriction naturally.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}Each cargo hold carries one unit. You may buy one unit per open hold.{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio defines the game's unit of traded cargo.
records.source_meaning: Julio says the amount that fills one cargo hold counts as one unit and purchases are limited by the number of cargo holds.
records.localization_note: Uses concise tutorial terminology while retaining the one-hold-to-one-unit rule.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}Market share also affects how much you can trade at once. The greater your share, the more you can trade.{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio introduces market share as a second trading limit.
records.source_meaning: Julio says market share changes the quantity that can be handled in one transaction and a higher share permits more trade.
records.localization_note: Market share is the established economic term; repetition keeps the rule clear.

records.english: Share?{PAD}
records.speaker: Raphael Castor
records.context: Raphael asks about the unfamiliar trading term.
records.source_meaning: Raphael repeats the word share as a question.
records.localization_note: Expands share to market share for clarity in American English.

records.english: Got it.{PAD}
records.speaker: Raphael Castor
records.context: Raphael acknowledges Julio's explanation.
records.source_meaning: Raphael says he understands.
records.localization_note: Brief, natural acknowledgment suited to a tutorial response.

records.english: How do we increase our market share?{PAD}
records.speaker: Raphael Castor
records.context: Raphael asks how the company can gain more market share.
records.source_meaning: Raphael asks how market share is increased.
records.localization_note: Uses we and our to avoid the unsafe standalone uppercase first-person glyph and fit the company context.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}Palaces and trading posts offer available shares to investors.{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio explains how investment grants market share.
records.source_meaning: Julio says that when market share is open, it is distributed to people who invest at the palace or trading post.
records.localization_note: Clearly connects investment with receiving available shares in natural tutorial language.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}Do not worry about that yet. Earn money and expand the fleet. Just try trading for now.{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio postpones the advanced share lesson and returns to the immediate tutorial.
records.source_meaning: Julio says share does not matter at first, since it becomes relevant after earning money and acquiring more ships, and tells Raphael to try trading now.
records.localization_note: Reorders the explanation into natural tutorial pacing and uses expand the fleet for acquiring more ships.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}Choose Confirm. Give it a try.{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio tells Raphael how to complete the trading interface.
records.source_meaning: Julio says to select the confirmation command when everything is satisfactory to end the transaction, then tells Raphael to try.
records.localization_note: Confirm is a concise interface label equivalent; transaction makes the action explicit.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}A ship needs sailors to move. We cannot manage her alone.{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio begins the sailor-recruitment tutorial.
records.source_meaning: Julio says nothing can begin until the ship can move, that the current group cannot operate it alone, and that sailors are necessary.
records.localization_note: Manage her uses natural nautical reference to the ship.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}Buy everyone drinks to attract sailors and show your generosity.{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio explains how buying drinks helps recruit sailors.
records.source_meaning: Julio says the trick to gathering sailors is to serve alcohol and demonstrate the admiral's great capacity or generosity.
records.localization_note: Generous admiral localizes the idiom about showing the size of one's character.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}At first, enough sailors will join even without drinks.{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio notes that the beginner fleet can recruit enough sailors without buying drinks.
records.source_meaning: Julio says receiving a drink creates goodwill, but early on the required number of sailors should gather without doing that.
records.localization_note: Keeps the beginner exception clear in natural spoken English after Julio's explanation of buying drinks.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}Choose Recruit Sailors and see who turns up.{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio directs Raphael to use the tavern recruitment command.
records.source_meaning: Julio tells Raphael to select the command for gathering sailors and wonders how many will come.
records.localization_note: Names the interface command and renders Julio's wondering about the result conversationally.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}Now assign the sailors. With only one ship, use the flagship option.{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio explains the sailor-allocation setting for a one-ship fleet.
records.source_meaning: Julio says sailors must finally be assigned and that the Favor Flagship setting is acceptable when the fleet has only one ship.
records.localization_note: Treats Favor Flagship as the named setting and phrases Julio's recommendation naturally.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}Extra sailors shorten how long your supplies last, so hire carefully.{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio warns about the supply cost of excess sailors.
records.source_meaning: Julio says increasing the sailor count shortens the fleet's sailing endurance and warns against hiring beyond the necessary number.
records.localization_note: Explains the practical supply consequence behind reduced sailing endurance without overstating the warning.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}Now try it.{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio hands the recruitment interface over to Raphael.
records.source_meaning: Julio tells Raphael to try it.
records.localization_note: A warm, concise tutorial prompt.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}Everything clear so far, {MACRO:FI}? Sea routes can be confusing. Want an explanation?{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio offers an optional explanation of sea routes.
records.source_meaning: Julio asks FI whether things have gone smoothly and offers to explain sea routes because they may be difficult to understand.
records.localization_note: Preserves Julio's warning that sea routes can be confusing and leads naturally into the player's choice.

records.english: Yes, please.{PAD}
records.speaker: Raphael Castor
records.context: Player choice to accept Julio's sea-route explanation.
records.source_meaning: Raphael says yes and asks Julio to explain.
records.localization_note: Clear, polite menu choice.

records.english: No, thanks. Got it.{PAD}
records.speaker: Raphael Castor
records.context: Player choice to decline the sea-route explanation.
records.source_meaning: Raphael says he is fine and understands.
records.localization_note: Reads as a complete, polite refusal within the fixed allocation.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}Contracts with neighboring towns or ports create a sea route.{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio defines how sea routes are established.
records.source_meaning: Julio says that contracting with nearby adjacent towns or ports creates a sea route between them.
records.localization_note: Uses passive tutorial phrasing to present the rule succinctly.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}We trade in Lisbon and Ceuta.{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio uses the company's current contracts as an example.
records.source_meaning: Julio says FO currently has contracts with the towns of Lisbon and Ceuta.
records.localization_note: Uses the natural present-tense phrasing for the company's current contracts without adding a runtime macro absent from the source-locked record.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}{MACRO:FO} has a sea route between neighboring Lisbon and Ceuta.{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio completes the Lisbon-Ceuta route example.
records.source_meaning: Julio says Lisbon and Ceuta are adjacent, which means FO possesses a sea route between them.
records.localization_note: States the example naturally and lets the company-name macro stand without an uncertain article.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}A captain, surveyor, and sea route let you use Auto Travel.{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio introduces the requirements for automatic travel.
records.source_meaning: Julio says automatic movement becomes available when the deck has a captain and surveyor assigned and a sea route exists.
records.localization_note: Auto Travel is a natural concise interface term for the movement command.

records.english: Auto Travel?{PAD}
records.speaker: Raphael Castor
records.context: Raphael asks about the newly introduced travel command.
records.source_meaning: Raphael repeats automatic movement as a question.
records.localization_note: Matches the localized interface term used in the preceding line.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}Choose a destination on a connected route. We navigators will handle the ship.{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio explains what automatic travel does.
records.source_meaning: Julio says that on a connected route the player need not issue each steering command; after a destination is chosen, the navigators operate the ship and move there.
records.localization_note: Keeps the connected-route condition and explains that the navigators take over ship handling.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}At departure, select Auto Travel, then a destination.{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio gives the menu steps for automatic travel.
records.source_meaning: Julio says to select automatic movement at the departure office and designate a destination on the route map.
records.localization_note: Names the departure office explicitly and presents the two menu steps in natural order within the fixed allocation.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}But...{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio pauses before revealing that the fleet lacks a surveyor.
records.source_meaning: Julio says, however, and trails off.
records.localization_note: Makes the transition's implied concern natural in English without inventing a new fact.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}No one here can serve as surveyor...{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio identifies the obstacle to using automatic travel.
records.source_meaning: Julio says the fleet has no one capable of becoming the surveyor.
records.localization_note: Serve as is natural role-assignment language.

records.english: {SPEAKER:05}All that big talk, and you can't even survey, old man?{PAD}
records.speaker: Claudio Manaus
records.context: Claudio mocks Julio for explaining a job he cannot currently perform.
records.source_meaning: Claudio calls Julio an old man, accuses him of acting important, and asks whether he cannot even survey.
records.localization_note: The contraction suits Claudio's casual mockery; old man is established teasing characterization, not kinship.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}A sextant from Lisbon will solve it.{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio responds to Claudio by requesting a sextant.
records.source_meaning: Julio reluctantly tells the group to go to Lisbon and buy a sextant, saying he can manage somehow if he has it.
records.localization_note: No helping it preserves Julio's reluctant concession before he explains that a sextant solves the problem.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}Do not forget to equip me with it.{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio stresses that the purchased sextant must be equipped on him.
records.source_meaning: Julio tells Raphael not to forget to use the Equip command to give him the sextant.
records.localization_note: Restores Julio as the singular equipment recipient and keeps Equip as the interface action.

records.english: Equip?{PAD}
records.speaker: Raphael Castor
records.context: Raphael asks what Julio means by equipping the item.
records.source_meaning: Raphael repeats the word equipment or equip as a question.
records.localization_note: Uses the interface verb established by Julio's instruction.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}Examine the item and you will see. Now head to Lisbon.{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio tells Raphael how to learn about equipment and resumes the objective.
records.source_meaning: Julio says carefully checking the purchased item will explain it and tells the group to head to Lisbon.
records.localization_note: Examine is concise game-action language and the objective is stated directly.

records.english: Y-yes.{PAD}
records.speaker: Raphael Castor
records.context: Raphael responds nervously to Julio's abrupt instruction.
records.source_meaning: Raphael stammers yes.
records.localization_note: Preserves the hesitation naturally.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}Good luck, then.{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio sends Raphael off to complete the tutorial objective.
records.source_meaning: Julio tells Raphael to work hard.
records.localization_note: Localizes the stock encouragement as a warm, concise send-off.

records.english: {SPEAKER:04}At a palace or governor's office, invest to fortify a town.{PAD}
records.speaker: Janus Pasar
records.context: Janus explains how military investment fortifies towns.
records.source_meaning: Janus says that investing at a palace or governor's office raises a town's armament level in preparation for enemy attacks.
records.localization_note: Preserves both investment locations and expresses the defense mechanic without unsafe literal macro bytes.

records.english: {SPEAKER:04}Portugal built eastern forts and used them as trading bases.{PAD}
records.speaker: Janus Pasar
records.context: Janus describes Portugal's overseas fortification strategy.
records.source_meaning: Janus says Portugal built fortresses in towns reaching the Indian Ocean and made them bases for trade.
records.localization_note: Conveys the long eastward reach and trading purpose naturally while avoiding the unsafe uppercase ASCII glyph in the source's ocean name.

records.english: {SPEAKER:04}That skill lets Portugal fortify towns for less than other nations.{PAD}
records.speaker: Janus Pasar
records.context: Janus explains Portugal's national advantage in fortification.
records.source_meaning: Janus says the construction techniques developed there should let Portugal raise town armament with less military investment than other countries.
records.localization_note: Expertise refers to the construction techniques Janus just described; fortify towns states the game effect directly.

records.english: Really? We'll remember that.{PAD}
records.speaker: Raphael Castor
records.context: Raphael acknowledges Janus's explanation of Portugal's advantage.
records.source_meaning: Raphael reacts with interest, says he understands, and promises to remember it.
records.localization_note: The contraction gives Raphael a natural response while we avoids the unsafe standalone uppercase first-person glyph.

records.english: {SPEAKER:05}Whoa! Look at this beauty!{PAD}
records.speaker: Claudio Manaus
records.context: Claudio reacts exuberantly to the newly arrived ship.
records.source_meaning: Claudio shouts in amazement that the ship is incredible.
records.localization_note: Look at this beauty gives his excitement a natural sailor's voice.

records.english: {SPEAKER:04}Th-this is a new ship of the line!{PAD}
records.speaker: Janus Pasar
records.context: Janus identifies the impressive vessel.
records.source_meaning: Janus stammers in surprise that it is a new-model ship of the line.
records.localization_note: Ship of the line is the precise historical term; new conveys the new model within the fixed allocation and the stammer preserves Janus's shock.

records.english: Amazing!{PAD}
records.speaker: Raphael Castor
records.context: Raphael marvels at the ship.
records.source_meaning: Raphael says it is amazing.
records.localization_note: Direct excited reaction.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}Hayreddin's parting gift...{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio recognizes who sent the ship.
records.source_meaning: Julio realizes the ship is a farewell gift from Hayreddin.
records.localization_note: Parting gift naturally conveys the farewell present.

records.english: Wh-what does that mean?{PAD}
records.speaker: Raphael Castor
records.context: Raphael asks what message Hayreddin intended.
records.source_meaning: Raphael stammers and wonders what the gift means.
records.localization_note: Preserves his startled hesitation.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}Maybe Spain isn't his real target...{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio suggests Hayreddin's gift carries a second political message.
records.source_meaning: Julio says the intended meaning is probably something more than a request to defeat Spain.
records.localization_note: Makes Julio's contrast explicit within the fixed allocation while preserving the suspense that Claudio resolves.

records.english: {SPEAKER:04}No way!{PAD}
records.speaker: Janus Pasar
records.context: Janus realizes Julio may mean opposition to the Ottomans.
records.source_meaning: Janus exclaims that it cannot be so.
records.localization_note: A compact natural exclamation preserves Janus's disbelief within the very small allocation.

records.english: What?!{PAD}
records.speaker: Raphael Castor
records.context: Raphael reacts to the implication about Hayreddin's enemies.
records.source_meaning: Raphael gives a startled exclamation.
records.localization_note: Direct natural reaction.

records.english: {SPEAKER:05}He expects us to beat the Ottomans.{PAD}
records.speaker: Claudio Manaus
records.context: Claudio bluntly states the implication of Hayreddin's gift.
records.source_meaning: Claudio says he understands and asks whether Hayreddin is telling them to destroy the Ottoman Turks.
records.localization_note: Beat suits Claudio's blunt voice and makes the group's implied role explicit without a needlessly literal ethnic formulation.

records.english: N-no! But...{PAD}
records.speaker: Raphael Castor
records.context: Raphael is alarmed by Claudio's conclusion but cannot dismiss it.
records.source_meaning: Raphael protests with a stammer and trails off with but.
records.localization_note: Keeps the interrupted, conflicted reaction.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}The Pasha may absorb Algiers into Ottoman ranks.{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio explains the political threat facing Hayreddin's pirates.
records.source_meaning: Julio says he cannot state it with certainty but has heard that the Pasha intends to incorporate the Algiers pirates into the Turkish military.
records.localization_note: Rumor says preserves Julio's explicit uncertainty while presenting the threatened annexation as one natural sentence.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}Barbarossa Hayreddin is a pirate king who serves no one...{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio describes Hayreddin's fierce independence.
records.source_meaning: Julio calls Barbarossa Hayreddin a solitary pirate king whose principle is to belong to no one.
records.localization_note: The relative clause states Hayreddin's creed and fierce independence naturally within the fixed allocation.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}He cannot openly defy Ottoman rule.{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio explains why Hayreddin needs Raphael to act indirectly.
records.source_meaning: Julio says Hayreddin cannot openly make an enemy of the Ottoman Turks.
records.localization_note: Names Hayreddin as the subject and states his political constraint in natural English.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}He must have sensed something special in {MACRO:FI}.{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio explains why Hayreddin entrusted the implied mission to Raphael.
records.source_meaning: Julio supposes Hayreddin sensed something within FI.
records.localization_note: Something special naturally conveys the favorable but undefined quality; macro preserved.

records.english: {SPEAKER:05}Heh. We have to live up to that trust. Right, {MACRO:FI}?{PAD}
records.speaker: Claudio Manaus
records.context: Claudio embraces Hayreddin's expectations and urges Raphael to agree.
records.source_meaning: Claudio says that after being trusted to such a degree they have no choice but to act, then asks FI to agree.
records.localization_note: Live up to that trust conveys Hayreddin's expectations naturally and preserves Claudio's direct appeal for FI's agreement.

records.english: ...Y-yeah.{PAD}
records.speaker: Raphael Castor
records.context: Raphael hesitantly agrees with Claudio.
records.source_meaning: Raphael stammers an uncertain yes.
records.localization_note: Punctuation preserves both pause and hesitation.

records.english: {SPEAKER:04}Time for an inspection.{PAD}
records.speaker: Janus Pasar
records.context: Janus turns from speculation to checking their new vessel.
records.source_meaning: Janus says he will perform an inspection.
records.localization_note: Gives Janus a natural understated transition without unsafe uppercase first-person text.

records.english: All right. No choice. Let's go, everyone!{PAD}
records.speaker: Raphael Castor
records.context: Raphael accepts the mission and rallies his companions.
records.source_meaning: Raphael says he understands that they have no choice but to act and calls everyone to go.
records.localization_note: Preserves Raphael's acceptance of necessity and renders his rally in youthful, natural English within the fixed allocation.
